entry.idea: Factory builds AI agents called Droids that take a plain-language coding task, such as "fix this bug", and carry out the whole job: finding the cause, writing the fix, testing it, and opening a pull request.
entry.lesson: Meet users inside the tools they already use instead of asking them to switch, and avoid locking your product to a single underlying AI model.
entry.name: Factory

growth.basis: substitute: valuation jumped from $1.5B to $5B between two funding rounds five months apart
growth.reason: Its valuation more than tripled in about five months, backed by a large new funding round from major investors.

market.reason: Every software team in the world writes and maintains code, so an AI agent that automates that work has a very large potential market.

tech.reason: Understanding a whole repository and shipping multi-file changes across many editors and channels is a real edge, but the AI coding-agent field is crowded and moving fast, so a strong rival team could match it within a year or two.

sources.title: AIコーディングエージェント「Droids」のFactory、評価額50億ドルで2億ドルを調達
Uma startup de droides de software vale agora US$ 5 bilhões

entry.twist: The agents work inside whatever tool a developer already uses, like VS Code, JetBrains, a terminal, a browser or Slack, and are not locked to a single AI model.
entry.who_pays: Software companies and development teams pay to use Factory's Droids inside their existing tools.
entry.why_now: AI models have become reliable enough to handle coding tasks that span many files in a repository from start to finish, so investors are racing to back the leading AI coding-agent companies.

mentions.snippet: Maker of the Droids AI coding agents; raised $200M at a $5B valuation.
